title: Binomial series expansion for relativistic gamma
seriesSpoken: Quantity one minus x to the power minus one half equals one plus half x plus three eighths x squared plus five sixteenths x cubed plus thirty-five over one hundred twenty-eight x to the fourth, followed by higher order terms.

explanation.text: The Lorentz factor gamma equals (1 - v^2/c^2)^(-1/2). For speeds v strictly less than the speed of light c, the variable x = (v/c)^2 satisfies |x| < 1. Expanding gamma in a binomial series reveals how relativistic kinetic terms connect directly to classical mechanics and mass-energy equivalence.

At v/c = 0.6 (where x = 0.36), the partial sums of gamma - 1 are: first term 0.18, through quadratic 0.2286, through cubic 0.24318, and through quartic 0.247773, converging toward the exact value 0.25. The leading quadratic term 0.18 corresponds to the 0.18L mass-energy fixture beside the exact 0.25L, demonstrating both the retained term and the neglected remainder.

At low speeds, floating-point subtraction gamma - 1 suffers from catastrophic subtractive cancellation. For example, at v/c = 10^(-4) (x = 10^(-8)), the exact value of gamma - 1 is 5.0000000375e-9, which matches the leading term 5.0e-9 to a relative difference of 7.5e-9. A cancellation-free evaluation using expm1 and log1p reproduces this exact value. In contrast, naive subtraction 1/sqrt(1-x) - 1 in standard double precision yields 5.0000001917e-9 with a relative error of 3.83e-8, five times too large. The cancellation-free route is required for trustworthy numerical evaluation.
